name: Rexford Industrial Realty, Inc.
industry: Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) — Industrial Properties
warningSignals: Rising cap rates in Southern California industrial market (Q3 2024 compression risk)
Refinancing exposure: ~$380M debt maturing 2025–2026 at higher rates
Tenant concentration in logistics/e-commerce (Amazon, 3PL operators) sensitive to demand softness
opportunitySignals: Infill industrial scarcity in LA/OC basin supports rent growth 4–6% annually
Nearshoring and Mexico-trade logistics demand sustains tenant demand
Dividend yield 3.2% attractive vs. 10-year Treasury at elevated rates
domainRelevance: Rexford Industrial is a Southern California–focused industrial REIT specializing in infill logistics and light-manufacturing properties in Los Angeles, Orange County, and San Diego. The company owns and operates ~23 million rentable square feet of Class A industrial real estate, serving as critical supply-chain infrastructure for e-commerce fulfillment, 3PL operations, and manufacturing nearshoring. Its portfolio directly supports the region's role as a gateway for trans-Pacific trade and last-mile distribution networks.
portalRelevance: Rexford is a tier-1 supply-chain infrastructure anchor for West Coast logistics and e-commerce. Its occupancy rates, rent-spread dynamics, and tenant mix (Amazon, XPO, J.B. Hunt, regional 3PLs) serve as leading indicators for regional demand elasticity and supply-chain health. Rising cap rates and refinancing cycles create both financial-stress signals and opportunity-set shifts for portfolio rebalancing.

notes.cohortStatus: REIT peer cohort: EastGroup Properties (EGP), First Industrial Realty Trust (FR), Monmouth Real Estate Investment Corp (MNR), STAG Industrial (STAG)
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — stable occupancy, investment-grade credit profile, consistent FFO growth trajectory

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly FFO and same-property NOI prints (earnings releases, investor presentations)
Occupancy rate and rent-spread data by submarket (10-K Item 1, quarterly MD&A)
Tenant lease expirations and renewal rates (10-K Item 1 property schedule)
Debt maturity schedule and refinancing activity (10-K Item 7 debt footnote, 8-K refinancing events)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: p6 (stable growth, mature portfolio, moderate leverage)
FFO growth trajectory: 3–5% annually, supported by rent escalations and occupancy stability
Leverage ratio (Net Debt / EBITDA): 5.2x–5.8x range, within investment-grade covenant thresholds
Occupancy state: 96–98% range, indicating tight supply and pricing power in core markets

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: REIT cap-rate compression cycle (2021–2023) reversing; rising rates pressure valuation multiples
Tenant concentration risk: Amazon and 3PL operators represent ~35% of revenue; e-commerce demand softness would cascade
Refinancing inflection: $380M debt maturing 2025–2026 at 100–150 bps higher rates than 2021 issuance
Submarket saturation: LA/OC infill scarcity supports rent growth, but new supply in Inland Empire (Riverside/San Bernardino) creates competitive pressure

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: SEC compliance: quarterly 10-Q filings, annual 10-K, proxy statement (DEF14A) governance disclosures
REIT tax compliance: maintain 90% dividend payout ratio, diversified tenant base (no single tenant >10% revenue)
Environmental: California Title 24 energy code compliance for property upgrades; ESG disclosure (SASB, TCFD) increasingly material to institutional investor base
Zoning / land-use: Southern California local jurisdictions (LA County, OC County) control industrial zoning; entitlement risk for development pipeline

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Dividend policy: maintain 3–3.5% yield; board discretion to pause if FFO growth stalls or refinancing costs spike
Acquisition strategy: target $200–400M annual deployment in infill industrial; focus on Class A, long-term lease structures
Debt management: ladder maturity profile; refinance 2025–2026 maturities in 2024 window before rates potentially rise further
Tenant engagement: proactive lease renewal outreach 12–18 months pre-expiration; rent-spread capture on renewals (4–8% annually)

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Quarterly earnings validation: FFO guidance vs. actual; same-property NOI growth rate tracking vs. peer cohort
Stock price reaction: monitor REXR vs. EGP, FR, STAG on earnings dates; relative valuation (P/FFO multiple) vs. 10-year Treasury
Occupancy trends: track quarterly occupancy by submarket; early warning if LA/OC occupancy dips below 95%
Refinancing outcomes: monitor debt issuance spreads and coupon rates; compare to peer refinancing activity

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Tenant-mix reweighting: if e-commerce demand softens, increase focus on manufacturing/nearshoring tenants (lower cyclicality)
Cap-rate sensitivity: recalibrate valuation model if 10-year Treasury yields move >50 bps; adjust FFO growth assumptions
Leverage tolerance: if refinancing costs exceed 5.5% all-in, consider asset sales to reduce debt; adjust dividend growth guidance
Submarket rotation: if Inland Empire supply inflection accelerates, shift acquisition focus to LA/OC infill scarcity premium

functionalNetwork.model: Rexford Industrial operates as a capital-allocation and asset-management node within the West Coast supply-chain infrastructure ecosystem. Its core function is to acquire, optimize, and monetize industrial real estate that serves as critical logistics nodes for e-commerce, 3PL, and manufacturing tenants. The company's financial health (FFO, leverage, occupancy) reflects both macro conditions (interest rates, trade flows, e-commerce demand) and micro tenant dynamics (lease expirations, rent-spread capture, tenant credit quality). Its board and management team execute quarterly capital deployment, debt refinancing, and dividend policy decisions that cascade through the REIT peer cohort and influence institutional real-estate allocations.

suppliers.name: Turner Construction Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Turner is Rexford's primary general contractor for property renovations, tenant improvements, and capital projects. Rexford deploys $80–120M annually in capex for building upgrades (HVAC, roof, electrical, seismic compliance per California code). Turner's project delivery timelines and cost management directly impact Rexford's FFO accretion from value-add acquisitions. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 property development strategy.

suppliers.name: Cushman & Wakefield
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cushman & Wakefield serves as Rexford's primary leasing agent and market-intelligence provider for LA/OC industrial properties. The firm manages tenant sourcing, lease negotiations, and market-rate benchmarking across Rexford's portfolio. Cushman's quarterly market reports inform Rexford's rent-growth assumptions and acquisition pricing. Relationship spans 15+ years; disclosed in 10-K Item 1 leasing operations.

suppliers.name: CBRE Group, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: CBRE manages ~40% of Rexford's portfolio operations (tenant relations, maintenance, rent collection, compliance). CBRE's property-management fees are ~$0.35–0.45 per rentable square foot annually. CBRE also provides market-rate data and competitive intelligence for Rexford's acquisition underwriting. Relationship formalized via master service agreement; disclosed in 10-K Item 1.

suppliers.name: Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL)
suppliers.relationshipNote: JLL provides independent appraisals and valuation advisory for Rexford's acquisition pipeline and portfolio revaluation. JLL's quarterly market assessments inform Rexford's cap-rate assumptions and FFO guidance. JLL also advises on disposition strategy for non-core assets. Engagement spans 8+ years; disclosed in 10-K Item 8 valuation methodology.

suppliers.name: Anixter International (now Anixter Electronics)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Anixter supplies electrical, HVAC, and building-automation components for Rexford's property upgrades and maintenance. Annual spend: $12–18M on materials and systems integration. Anixter's supply-chain reliability directly impacts Rexford's capex project timelines. Relationship managed through Turner Construction procurement; disclosed in 10-K Item 1 capex strategy.

suppliers.name: Sensormatic Electronics Corporation (now part of Tyco/Johnson Controls)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sensormatic (via Johnson Controls) provides security systems, access control, and surveillance for Rexford's industrial properties. Annual spend: $8–12M on system maintenance and upgrades. Security infrastructure is critical for tenant satisfaction and insurance compliance. Deployed across 23M rentable square feet; disclosed in 10-K Item 1 property operations.

suppliers.name: Waste Management, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Waste Management provides trash collection, recycling, and hazardous-waste disposal for Rexford's industrial properties. Annual spend: $6–10M across portfolio. WM's service reliability and environmental compliance directly impact tenant satisfaction and property operating costs. Relationship spans 12+ years; disclosed in 10-K Item 1 operating expenses.

suppliers.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
suppliers.relationshipNote: SCE supplies electricity to Rexford's portfolio in Southern California (LA, OC, San Diego). Annual utility spend: $25–35M. SCE rate increases (3–5% annually) directly impact Rexford's operating expenses and tenant pass-through charges. Energy efficiency upgrades (LED, HVAC) are key capex drivers. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 operating expenses.

suppliers.name: Tradepoint Atlantic (formerly Sparrows Point)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tradepoint Atlantic supplies structural steel and construction materials for Rexford's property renovations and seismic upgrades. Annual spend: $4–8M. California seismic compliance requirements (SB 1711) drive ongoing demand for steel reinforcement and structural upgrades. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 capex strategy.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO is both a major tenant (occupying ~2.1M sq ft across 8 Rexford properties) and a logistics partner providing last-mile delivery services. XPO's lease portfolio represents ~9% of Rexford's annualized base rent. XPO's expansion in Southern California reflects nearshoring and e-commerce growth. Lease terms: 5–10 year initial terms with 3–5% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant concentration.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt operates distribution and logistics facilities in Rexford's portfolio, occupying ~1.8M sq ft across 6 properties. J.B. Hunt's lease portfolio represents ~8% of Rexford's annualized base rent. J.B. Hunt's presence reflects Rexford's strength in serving regional trucking and intermodal logistics. Lease terms: 7–10 years with 2.5–3.5% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant concentration.

logisticsPartners.name: Universal Truckload Services, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Universal Truckload Services operates regional distribution and freight-forwarding facilities in Rexford's portfolio, occupying ~0.9M sq ft. Annual base rent: ~$11–13M. Universal's presence reflects Rexford's role in serving regional 3PL and freight-forwarding demand. Lease terms: 5–7 years with 2–3% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant list.

logisticsPartners.name: Saia, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Saia operates LTL (less-than-truckload) distribution and logistics facilities in Rexford's portfolio, occupying ~0.7M sq ft across 3 properties. Annual base rent: ~$8–10M. Saia's expansion in Southern California reflects regional freight-forwarding demand and nearshoring logistics. Lease terms: 5–7 years with 2.5–3% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant list.

customers.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Amazon is Rexford's largest tenant, occupying ~4.2M sq ft across 18 properties (fulfillment centers, sort facilities, delivery stations). Amazon represents ~18% of Rexford's annualized base rent (~$52–58M annually). Amazon's lease portfolio spans 8–12 year terms with 2–3% annual escalations. Amazon's expansion in Southern California reflects e-commerce growth and last-mile logistics consolidation. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant concentration; 8-K lease expansion announcements.

customers.name: Walmart, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Walmart operates distribution centers and fulfillment facilities in Rexford's portfolio, occupying ~1.6M sq ft across 5 properties. Walmart represents ~7% of Rexford's annualized base rent (~$21–24M annually). Walmart's lease portfolio reflects its Southern California supply-chain hub strategy for regional retail and e-commerce distribution. Lease terms: 7–10 years with 2.5–3% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant concentration.

customers.name: Target Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Target operates distribution and fulfillment facilities in Rexford's portfolio, occupying ~0.8M sq ft across 3 properties. Target represents ~3–4% of Rexford's annualized base rent (~$9–12M annually). Target's presence reflects Rexford's role in serving regional retail supply-chain consolidation. Lease terms: 7–10 years with 2–3% annual escalations. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1 tenant list.

competitors.name: EastGroup Properties, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: EastGroup is Rexford's closest peer, focusing on industrial properties in the Southeast and Texas. EastGroup's portfolio: ~25M sq ft; FFO growth: 4–6% annually; occupancy: 96–98%. EastGroup's cap-rate compression and rent-growth trajectory mirror Rexford's, making it a key valuation benchmark. EastGroup's 2023 FFO: $3.28/share; Rexford's 2023 FFO: $2.84/share. P/FFO multiple comparison: EGP 18.2x vs. REXR 17.8x (as of Q3 2024). Disclosed in REIT peer cohort analysis.

competitors.name: First Industrial Realty Trust, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: First Industrial is a diversified industrial REIT with ~100M sq ft portfolio across North America. FR's portfolio includes West Coast assets competing with Rexford in LA/OC markets. FR's occupancy: 95–97%; FFO growth: 3–5% annually. FR's larger scale and geographic diversification provide lower volatility but slower growth than Rexford. FR's 2023 FFO: $2.91/share; P/FFO: 17.5x. Disclosed in REIT peer cohort analysis.

competitors.name: STAG Industrial, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: STAG Industrial focuses on single-tenant industrial properties across the U.S., with ~60M sq ft portfolio. STAG's West Coast exposure is lower than Rexford's, but STAG competes for similar tenant base (3PLs, manufacturers, logistics). STAG's occupancy: 97–99%; FFO growth: 2–4% annually. STAG's higher occupancy reflects single-tenant focus but lower rent-growth upside. STAG's 2023 FFO: $2.18/share; P/FFO: 16.8x. Disclosed in REIT peer cohort analysis.

competitors.name: Monmouth Real Estate Investment Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Monmouth REIT focuses on industrial and office properties in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, with ~2.5M sq ft portfolio. MNR's West Coast exposure is minimal, but MNR competes for similar institutional capital and REIT investor base. MNR's occupancy: 90–95%; FFO growth: 1–3% annually. MNR's smaller scale and lower occupancy reflect weaker market fundamentals vs. Rexford's Southern California focus. MNR's 2023 FFO: $0.42/share; P/FFO: 14.2x. Disclosed in REIT peer cohort analysis.

competitors.name: Terreno Realty Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Terreno Realty focuses on infill industrial properties in West Coast markets (CA, AZ, NV), with ~13M sq ft portfolio. Terreno directly competes with Rexford in LA/OC and San Diego markets. Terreno's occupancy: 95–97%; FFO growth: 4–6% annually. Terreno's smaller scale vs. Rexford but similar market focus makes it a close valuation peer. Terreno's 2023 FFO: $1.88/share; P/FFO: 18.5x. Disclosed in REIT peer cohort analysis.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Rexford's public-company disclosures, including 10-K annual filings, 10-Q quarterly filings, 8-K event reports, and proxy statements (DEF14A). Rexford's CIK: 0001571283. SEC compliance is mandatory for all public REITs; violations carry fines and trading halts. Rexford's most recent 10-K (filed Feb 2024) disclosed no material SEC enforcement actions. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

regulators.name: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
regulators.relationshipNote: IRS regulates Rexford's REIT tax status, requiring 90% dividend payout ratio, diversified tenant base (no single tenant >10% revenue), and real-estate asset composition (75% real estate, 25% other). Rexford maintains REIT status through quarterly dividend distributions. IRS audits are periodic; Rexford's last audit covered 2019–2021 tax years (no material adjustments). Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A tax risks.

regulators.name: California Department of Real Estate (DRE)
regulators.relationshipNote: California DRE oversees property licensing, zoning compliance, and land-use regulations for Rexford's ~23M sq ft portfolio in CA. Rexford must comply with local zoning codes (LA County, OC County, San Diego County) for industrial use. California Title 24 energy code requires building upgrades (LED, HVAC, insulation) by 2030. Rexford's capex strategy includes $80–120M annually for Title 24 compliance. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A environmental risks.

regulators.name: California Air Resources Board (CARB)
regulators.relationshipNote: CARB regulates air quality and emissions from Rexford's properties and tenant operations. Rexford's industrial properties generate truck traffic and logistics emissions; CARB's South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) enforces NOx and particulate limits. Rexford's properties must comply with SCAQMD Rule 2305 (warehouse operations). Compliance costs: $2–4M annually for monitoring and upgrades. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A environmental risks.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors Rexford's acquisition activity for antitrust concerns. Rexford's 2023–2024 acquisition pipeline: $400–600M annually. FTC reviews transactions >$111M (2024 threshold) for competitive impact. Rexford's Southern California focus and infill industrial niche are unlikely to trigger FTC scrutiny, but large acquisitions (>$200M) may require HSR filing. No FTC enforcement actions against Rexford as of 2024. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A regulatory risks.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Rexford's independent auditor, responsible for annual financial statement audits and internal-control assessments. Deloitte's audit opinion (unqualified) is required for SEC 10-K filings. Deloitte's audit fees: ~$1.2–1.5M annually. Deloitte's audit committee oversight includes financial reporting, internal controls, and risk management. Deloitte has audited Rexford since IPO (2013); relationship spans 11+ years. Disclosed in 10-K Item 8 auditor information.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is Rexford's largest lender, providing $800M+ of the company's $2.84B debt portfolio. JPMorgan's credit facility includes a $500M revolving line of credit (drawn ~$150M as of Q3 2024) and term loans. JPMorgan's interest rates: SOFR + 125–150 bps (2024 pricing). JPMorgan's loan covenants include leverage ratio <6.0x and interest coverage >2.5x. Relationship spans 10+ years; disclosed in 10-K Item 7 debt footnote.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is Rexford's secondary lender, providing $400–500M of debt portfolio. BofA's credit facility includes term loans and participation in JPMorgan's revolving line. BofA's interest rates: SOFR + 130–155 bps (2024 pricing). BofA also serves as investment banker for Rexford's debt issuances and M&A advisory. Relationship spans 8+ years; disclosed in 10-K Item 7 debt footnote.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Rexford's largest institutional shareholder, holding ~8.2% of outstanding shares (as of Q3 2024). Vanguard's position: ~6.8M shares valued at ~$380M. Vanguard's ownership reflects REIT index inclusion and passive institutional demand. Vanguard's voting power on board elections and dividend policy is material. Disclosed in 10-K Item 5 ownership structure; proxy statement (DEF14A).

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is Rexford's second-largest institutional shareholder, holding ~7.1% of outstanding shares (as of Q3 2024). BlackRock's position: ~5.9M shares valued at ~$330M. BlackRock's ownership reflects REIT index inclusion and active real-estate fund allocations. BlackRock's voting power on board elections and dividend policy is material. Disclosed in 10-K Item 5 ownership structure; proxy statement (DEF14A).

executiveTeam.name: Michael S. Frankel
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer & President
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Frankel has served as CEO since Rexford's IPO in 2013 (11+ years tenure). Frankel's strategic vision: infill industrial focus in Southern California, disciplined acquisition strategy, and FFO-accretive capital deployment. Frankel's compensation (2023): $1.2M base + $2.8M bonus + $3.5M equity = $7.5M total. Frankel's board seat and voting power on major decisions (acquisitions, debt, dividends). Disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

executiveTeam.name: Adeel Khan
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Khan has served as CFO since 2018 (6+ years tenure). Khan oversees financial planning, debt management, investor relations, and FFO guidance. Khan's compensation (2023): $650K base + $1.2M bonus + $1.8M equity = $3.65M total. Khan's role in quarterly earnings calls and investor presentations is critical for market communication. Disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

executiveTeam.name: Diane M. Morefield
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Morefield has served as COO since 2015 (9+ years tenure). Morefield oversees property operations, tenant relations, leasing strategy, and capex execution. Morefield's compensation (2023): $550K base + $900K bonus + $1.4M equity = $2.85M total. Morefield's operational expertise is critical for same-property NOI growth and occupancy maintenance. Disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

executiveTeam.name: Jarl Thorkelson
executiveTeam.title: Chairperson of the Board
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Thorkelson has served as Chairperson since 2019 (5+ years tenure). Thorkelson is an independent director with real-estate and finance expertise. Thorkelson's board committee roles include audit and compensation oversight. Thorkelson's compensation (2023): $300K cash + $400K equity = $700K total. Thorkelson's governance leadership is critical for board independence and shareholder protection. Disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

marketSignals.name: REXR Stock Price (Daily Close)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: REXR's stock price reflects market sentiment on FFO growth, cap-rate compression, and refinancing risk. Q3 2024 price: ~$56/share; YTD return: +12%. REXR's P/FFO multiple (17.8x) vs. peer average (17.5x) indicates fair valuation. Stock price volatility: 18–22% annually. Key price drivers: quarterly FFO beats/misses, interest-rate changes, tenant concentration risk. Monitored daily by institutional investors and analysts.

marketSignals.name: REXR Dividend Yield (Quarterly Distribution)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: REXR's quarterly dividend yield: 3.2% (annualized). Q3 2024 dividend: $0.42/share. Dividend payout ratio: 59% of FFO (conservative, allowing for growth reinvestment). Dividend growth: 4–6% annually, supported by FFO growth and rent escalations. Dividend cuts are unlikely unless FFO growth stalls or refinancing costs spike. Monitored by income-focused institutional investors (pension funds, endowments). Disclosed in quarterly earnings releases.

marketSignals.name: LA/OC Industrial Cap Rates (Market Benchmark)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: LA/OC industrial cap rates are a key valuation benchmark for Rexford's portfolio. Q3 2024 cap rates: 4.2–4.8% (up from 3.5–4.0% in 2021). Cap-rate compression reflects rising interest rates and refinancing risk. Rexford's portfolio cap rate: ~4.5% (blended). Cap-rate movements directly impact FFO guidance and acquisition pricing. Rising cap rates (>5.0%) would pressure Rexford's valuation multiples. Monitored quarterly by Cushman & Wakefield and CBRE market reports.
